- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then overshoot, followed by a sharp drop — suggesting overreaction to short-term volatility.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift upward after initial spikes, then sharply correct downward, often missing the true mean.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 2–5 days in the early part of the 30d window, then catch up or overshoot.
- When true values show a downward trend, model forecasts often remain elevated, failing to adjust to the trend.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, suggesting a “tail risk” or horizon bias.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent spikes — model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, leading to overcorrection.
- Model fails to capture long-term mean reversion in the 30d window — tends to hold forecasts above true mean for extended periods.
- Forecasts often overshoot after a spike, then correct too abruptly — suggesting a “reversion-to-mean” heuristic is misapplied.
- Model underestimates prices when true values are trending downward — fails to recognize downward momentum early.
